what_happened.line: The Commission voted a positive determination on the Lake Shirley Dam maintenance path request, which means the project must file a notice of intent.
The applicant was asked to check whether the town holds easement rights over Fire Road 19 to the dam.
The Commission approved a third-party reviewer, Ecotech, for 390 Howard Street, contingent on staff confirming Ecotech knows of the site disturbance.
The Commission approved notices of intent for septic work, a driveway and wall, and a lot on Kilburn Street, and continued two hearings to March 6.
The Commission reached a consensus to stay fully remote, and extended the Lake Shirley order of conditions by three years.

why_it_matters: The Lake Shirley dam path now needs a full notice of intent, which means a fuller wetlands review and a public hearing before work on the dam can proceed.
The third-party reviewer at 390 Howard Street would be paid through a town 53G account that the applicant funds, so the review is meant to be paid for by the applicant.
Staying remote affects how residents attend and comment on Conservation Commission hearings, and the commission has said it will tell the select board it prefers that.
watch_next: The continued hearings for 255 Sunny Hill Road and 171 Arbor Street, set for March 6.
The notice of intent filing for the Lake Shirley dam path, and whether the town holds easement rights over Fire Road 19.
